newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's YUKOS oil eyes stock issue, share split.
newsitem.headline: Russia's YUKOS oil eyes stock issue, share split.

text.p: Shareholders of Russia's NK YUKOS oil company, parent of Yuganskneftegaz, will consider a 35 percent capital increase to pay off debts in an extraordinary meeting on Saturday, the company said on Friday.
A spokesman said the YUKOS board had recommended a 250-1 share split, giving new shares a nominal value of four roubles.
It also recommended a new issue of 580 million shares nominally worth a total 2.3 billion roubles.
"The specific volume of the issue will be determined by the board of directors on September 28," the spokesman said.
YUKOS needs funds to pay wage arrears and debts to the federal budget.
The spokesman did not give a figure for the company's debt, but Russian news agencies said it may be 1.8 trillion roubles.
YUKOS' nominal capital is 6.6 billion roubles.
AOOT NK YUKOS is one of around a dozen vertically integrated oil companies set up in recent years.
Its Yuganskneftegaz unit is Russia's second-largest oil producer.
In a December 1995 shares-for-loans auction of government assets, Russia's Bank Menatep won a 33 percent stake in YUKOS and the right to manage an additional 45 percent. ($1 = 5,376 roubles)
